explanation: Include the new interval, sort by start, then extend the last result while closed intervals overlap or touch. Copy result rows rather than changing the supplied intervals.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) time for n input intervals.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: After sorting by start, the output contains the union of all intervals processed so far. A new interval overlaps the final output interval exactly when its start does not exceed that interval’s end; extending the end preserves the union. Otherwise it starts a separated component. Including the new interval in this sweep yields the complete updated union.
walkthrough: Insert [2,7] into [[0,2],[6,8]]. Closed intervals [0,2] and [2,7] touch and merge to [0,7]. That range overlaps [6,8], so the final result is [[0,8]].
edgeCases: Input intervals are sorted, disjoint closed ranges.
Touching endpoints merge in this collection.
The new interval may bridge several original intervals.
